doc: Model assumptions per facts bundle (whitepaper §8.5, §8.6, Def 4.7). A result record lists, in model_assumptions, every entry whose introduced_by meets the cone of its law: the model definitions the frozen statement reaches. Every definition of a bundle's generated model is classified: by one or more entries (entries take precedence), or else by exactly one no_assumption group with its reason. Patterns are fnmatch globs over definition names; "*" in introduced_by means every law of the bundle. Kinds: hash (a collision-freedom stand-in, Cor 6.16), oracle (a neighbour or runtime replaced by a stand-in), hypothesis (a constant or oracle claim checkable outside the model), abstraction (a representation choice of the model), scope_note (what the bundle does not cover). Statement premises (assume clauses) are not here: they are in the frozen IR and in each record's premises.

entries.text: batchIndex, l1MessagePopped, totalL1MessagePopped and lastBlockNumber are < 2^64 and modelled as 8-byte fields; Solidity stores shl(192, x) of a uint256, so larger values would be truncated.
The version field is one byte in the Header record.
Go encoders are modelled with an empty EncodedBytes cache.
Solidity encodes into memory at the free pointer whose prior contents are unknown; the model marks unwritten bytes UNKNOWN (0xDEAD, outside the byte range).
M0 compares header bytes, not hashes; no hash premise is used.

no_assumption.why: byte-list and equality utilities of the generator prelude; no modelling choice
field projections of the Header record, generated from the facts types

transcribed from the facts functions, which were checked by hand against morph 3e44e79 (replay/M0/facts_audit.md); ok_go and ok_sol are replayed on the L_dom_hdr witness only; fidelity of enc_sol and the dec_go defs is not measured yet (refinement_refs, I16; Solidity commit-path replays, I4)

entries.text: State roots, hashes and versioned hashes are Nat tokens (0 is bytes32(0)); times are Nat seconds from an epoch.

CF(keccak256, {stored headers, presented header}): header equality stands for committedBatches equality; a caller presents the stored header of the index it names, and committedBatches[k] != 0 iff k <= LCI (abstractions/2).
Per-batch registers live in a window (LFI..LCI) and shadow lists (LCI+1, ...: residues of revertBatch); finalized indices keep only committedBatches and finalizedStateRoots.
challenges and finalizedStateRoots are arrays indexed by absolute batch index.
keccak256 over the blob versioned hashes (version 2) is the injective stand-in agg(xs) = AGG_BASE + enc(xs): CF(keccak256, S) for every finite S.

Token Z stands for ZERO_VERSIONED_HASH (Rollup.sol:25), assumed equal to the KZG versioned hash of the all-zero blob, 0x01 || sha256(0xc0 || 0^47)[1:] (D2, whitepaper §11.6). The facts' constants_doc cites Rollup.sol:24 and says the value is oracle-checked by holon; no code in the repo performed that check before I3. Not the compression hypothesis HypZ of §8.5. laws/M1/L_fact_Z.json's notes repeat the wrong text ("HypZ ... oracle-checked", CF as a premise); the frozen-statement file is left untouched in I1 (its notes are not hashed) and corrected with the statement lifecycle (I10).
ISubmitter is a stand-in: isActive is membership of the active list, challengeDeposit = DEP, and _challengerWin's slash removes the batch submitter from the active list.
IRollupVerifier is a stand-in that accepts iff proof == 1.
The cross-domain messenger is a stand-in: sendMessage appends one message to the queue.
Not modelled: reward and deposit accounting, withdrawalRoots, parameter updates, challenger and verifier admin, importGenesisBatch, initialize3/4, dataHash contents (facts coverage.debt).
The initial state s0 is the state after initialize(...) and importGenesisBatch at t = 10, with parameters W = 10, F = 40, D = 20, active = [2, 3], challengers = [4].
The pre-reinitializer(2) state is emulated by a pseudo-migration that zeroes committedStateRoots in a state reached by the current version's actions; it is not a versioned machine.
Discharge costs are per-action constants: one L1 message = 1, one validity proof = 1000 (c_proof >> c_msg); delay is time waited.
The obligated class of a DISCH law is derived from each action's free-text principal label (perm: true for actions open to anyone or the environment), not from a permission predicate over callers.

entries.text: The Go heap is a list of backing arrays of Nat bytes; a slice is (backing, offset, len, cap); append writes in place when len + k <= cap and allocates otherwise.
Go 1.24 slice growth (nextslicecap plus roundupsize) with the size-class table truncated to classes <= 512 bytes; larger allocations use the exact requested capacity, which is wrong for real Go.
NewBatchData's make([]byte, 0) slices start with capacity 0 and no backing array.
l1TxHashes, blockNum and l1TxNum are not modelled.
